newsitem.title: USA: Home Depot sees '97 EPS growth of 23-25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Home Depot sees '97 EPS growth of 23-25 pct.

text.p: Home Depot Inc, the largest home-improvement retailer in North America with 536 stores, said it was comfortable with earnings per share growth estimates of 23 to 25 percent for the year.

"We said at the end of last year and at the end of our first quarter that we are comfortable with earnings per share growth estimates of 23 to 25 percent for the year," Marshall Day, Home Depot's chief financial officer, said in an interview after a presentation at a Piper Jaffray investment conference in Minneapolis.
For its fiscal year ended February 2, 1997, the Atlanta, Georgia-based retailer reported earnings of $1.94 a share on sales of $19.53 billion.
Day also said Home Depot was "on track" to add 111 stores this year, some of them in new markets such as Kansas City, Missouri, and Ottawa.
Earlier this month, Home Depot formalized a venture with S.A.C.I. Falabella, a Chilean department store operator, to open stores in that country. Home Depot controls 66.67 percent of the venture.
At that time, the U.S. company said the venture in Chile, its first outside of North America, would "serve as a platform for Home Depot's growth into other Latin American countries."
The venture, Home Depot Chile, plans to open a total of seven or eight stores in Chile, with the first one scheduled for 1998. The merchandise offered will be tailored to that country's needs.

In the United States, Home Depot has decided against implementing a nationwide program to sell free-standing appliances such as refrigerators, washers and dryers. The retailer will continue selling built-in appliances in conjunction with its kitchen cabinet sales.
In April, Home Depot President Arthur Blank said the retailer was considering the addition of a full line of appliances to its existing merchandise offerings.
